# Example Output — Remote MCP Server

*Generated by applying the Remote MCP Server skill to `example-input.md`.*

---

## 1. Topology

```text
ChatGPT / Claude
   │  https://mcp.example.com/mcp
   ▼
Cloudflare Worker  gardentrack-mcp-proxy        (custom domain attached in the dashboard)
   │  drops Authorization, apikey, Cookie and any caller X-Client-IP
   │  sets X-Client-IP from CF-Connecting-IP
   ▼
Supabase edge function  gardentrack-mcp
   https://<your-project-ref>.supabase.co/functions/v1/gardentrack-mcp
```

- The server stays where it is. Only its public address changes.
- `mcp.example.com` is attached to the Worker in the Cloudflare dashboard. `wrangler.toml` has no `routes` or custom-domain entry, so `wrangler deploy` ships code only and cannot change DNS.
- The function's `verify_jwt` setting and deploy flags follow `supabase-edge-functions`.

## 2. Proxy routes

| Path | Handling | Response |
|---|---|---|
| `/mcp` (any method) | Forwarded to the edge function, with caller `Authorization`, `apikey` and `Cookie` dropped | The upstream response, streamed through |
| `/.well-known/openai-apps-challenge` | Answered by the Worker from the secret `OPENAI_APPS_CHALLENGE` | `200 text/plain` with the token only, or `404` while the secret is unset |
| Anything else | Not forwarded | `404` |

## 3. Domain verification

- **Path:** `https://mcp.example.com/.well-known/openai-apps-challenge`. This is at the host root, not under `/mcp`.
- **Secret:** stored with `wrangler secret put OPENAI_APPS_CHALLENGE`. Nothing is committed to git.
- **Self-check:** before the secret was set, `404`, as expected. After it was set, `200` with `content-type: text/plain`, and the body is exactly the token, with no HTML and no surrounding whitespace.
- **Directory status:** check requested. Confirm that the portal shows `mcp.example.com` as verified before you submit.

## 4. Tool manifest

| Tool | `title` | `readOnlyHint` | `destructiveHint` | `openWorldHint` | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `find_stalls` | Find produce stalls | `true` | `false` | `false` | Reads GardenTrack's own database only |
| `get_stall` | Get stall details | `true` | `false` | `false` | Reads GardenTrack's own database only |
| `list_suburbs` | List suburbs with stalls | `true` | `false` | `false` | Reads GardenTrack's own database only |

All four fields are set explicitly on every tool. A `tools/list` request through `mcp.example.com` returns them.

## 5. Output sanitisation

Withheld: street numbers, in every form. In a `find_stalls` result, they appear in three payloads:

| Payload | Field | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model-visible text | One sentence per stall | Sanitised, but "No.88" got through | Shared sanitiser |
| `structuredContent` | `stalls[].address` | Raw row: `No.88 Hill St, Eastvale` | Shared sanitiser |
| Widget `_meta` | `markers[].popup` | Raw row | Shared sanitiser |

**Fix:** `sanitiseAddress()` runs once over each row's `address`, and the text, `structuredContent` and `_meta` are all built from the sanitised rows. `get_stall` uses the same path.

**Rules:**

- "No" and "No." with or without a space before the digits: `/\bNo\.?\s*\d+[A-Za-z]?\b/i`. The old pattern used `\s+`, which let "No.88" through.
- Leading numbers and unit forms: `88 Hill St`, `88A Hill St`, `4/88 Hill St`.

**Test cases:**

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| `88 Hill St, Eastvale` | `Hill St, Eastvale` |
| `88A Hill St, Eastvale` | `Hill St, Eastvale` |
| `4/88 Hill St, Eastvale` | `Hill St, Eastvale` |
| `No 88 Hill St, Eastvale` | `Hill St, Eastvale` |
| `No. 88 Hill St, Eastvale` | `Hill St, Eastvale` |
| `No.88 Hill St, Eastvale` | `Hill St, Eastvale` |
| `Hill St, Eastvale` | unchanged |

**Whole-result test:** a fixture stall at `No.8817 Hill St`. The serialised `find_stalls` result must not contain `8817` anywhere.

## 6. Widget behaviour

1. The widget loads and completes `ui/initialize` with the host.
2. Only then does it wait for the `find_stalls` result. Before the fix, it listened for the result as soon as it loaded, before the handshake had finished.
3. It starts the map library and draws markers from `_meta.markers`.
4. If the map library cannot start (for example, the CDN is blocked or the script throws), it shows the static PNG `fallback-map.png` instead of a blank frame.

**Hosts tested:** Claude, where it renders. ChatGPT still needs testing before submission.

## 7. Rate limiting

- **Key:** the platform's connecting IP. When the connecting IP is the Worker's egress, the key is `X-Client-IP`, which the Worker sets from `CF-Connecting-IP` after deleting any caller copy. `X-Forwarded-For` is never read. For reading the connecting IP inside the function, see `supabase-edge-functions`.
- **Limits:** 30 requests/min per caller, and a shared ceiling of 600 requests/min.
- **Order:** per-caller first, then shared. Before the fix, two things were wrong. The shared ceiling was checked first, so requests that were already over their own limit still used up the shared budget. And rotating `X-Forwarded-For` gave a single client a fresh per-caller limit on every request.

## 8. Pre-submission checks

| Check | How | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `/mcp` on the custom domain | MCP `initialize` and `tools/list` against `https://mcp.example.com/mcp` | 3 tools, all annotated |
| Caller credentials dropped | Request with `Authorization`, `apikey` and `Cookie` set; function logs incoming header names | None of the three present |
| Other paths closed | `curl -i https://mcp.example.com/` | `404` |
| Verification token | `curl -i https://mcp.example.com/.well-known/openai-apps-challenge` | `200 text/plain`, token only |
| Forged `X-Forwarded-For` | Two requests from one client, with `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.9` and `198.51.100.7` | Same rate-limit key |
| No street numbers | Whole-result fixture test, plus the sanitiser test cases | Pass |
| Widget fallback | Block the map library's CDN in browser dev tools | Static PNG shown |
| Directory verification | Directory portal | Confirm verified before submitting |
